capitals.name: Béjaïa (Bougie)
capitals.note: Abu Zakariya's seat in 1283-1301 and the emirs' seat in 1366-1370 and 1501-1510; the 1555 page calls Bougie 'the former capital of the dissident Hafsid emirs'. Constantine had its own prince (Abu Bakr in 1510) and is not entered.

correction.text: Béjaïa, Constantine, Algiers and Dellys, with Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page has no area; 'recognised as ruler not only in Béjaïa but in Constantine, Algiers and Dellys' (after 1283, undated) and 'Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès' (undated) are drawn from 1285, the infobox secession year. The Marinid capture of Algiers under Abu Yaqub Yusuf is undated on the page and not subtracted.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II secured control of Tunis and ceded Béjaïa to his cousin Abu Abdullah ibn Abu Zaria'; no year, after the Marinid invasion of 1347. 1350 is the researcher's bridge. The shape ignores Algiers, Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès, for which the page gives nothing after 1318.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In the early 16th century, the emir of Béjaïa was independent of Tunis' (HB page, no year); the Capture page has Abdelaziz at Béjaïa and his brother Abu Bakr as prince at Constantine. 1501 is my bridge; 1370-1500 is left without a shape (reunited under Tunis).

region.text: Béjaïa, Constantine, Algiers and Dellys, with Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès

ledger.note: 1285: Béjaïa and Constantine secede from the Hafsid domain of Ifriqiya. The infobox gives 'secession from Hafsid domain of Ifriqiya: 1285'; the text has Ibrahim and Abu Zakariya flee Béjaïa in 1283 and, after Ibn Abi Umara's rebellion, 'Abu Zakariya was recognised as ruler not only in Béjaïa but in Constantine, Algiers and Dellys' (no year); Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès were consolidated under him (no year).

1309: Abu-l-Baqa takes Tunis. 'When Abu Asida died in 1309 the sheikhs of Tunis proclaimed a son of Abu Faris bin Ibrahim I'; 'It took Abu-l Baqa seventeen days to eliminate his rival and take over Tunis.'

1310 (bridge): Tunis is lost again. 'No sooner was Abu-l Baqa installed in Tunis than rebellion broke out in Constantine, led by his own brother'; he surrendered and 'was quickly assassinated' (no year). The page gives no date for the loss of Tunis.

region.text: Béjaïa, Constantine, Algiers and Dellys, with Biskra, Ouargla and the Aurès

ledger.note: Early 1318: the Hafsid domains are reunited. 'In early 1318 Abu-Yahya Abu-Bakr made his entrance into the capital, thereby once again reuniting the Hafsid domains.' The page does not say in so many words that Béjaïa was reunited; it has Abu Bakr 'continue to rule in Béjaïa' while he lost Tunis.

1350 (bridge): Béjaïa is ceded to a cousin. 'Eventually Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II secured control of Tunis and ceded Béjaïa to his cousin Abu Abdullah ibn Abu Zaria'; the page gives no year, only the Marinid invasion of 1347 before it and May 1366 after it.

May 1366: Abu'l Abbas takes Béjaïa from Abu Abdullah. 'In May 1366 Abu'l Abbas took Béjaïa from him, thereby uniting western Ifriqiya under a single ruler once again'; a change of ruling line inside the branch.
1370: the western and eastern domains are reunited a third time. 'Abu'l Abbas was quickly able to reunite the western and eastern domains, for the third time, in 1370.'

Early 16th century (bridge, 1501): Béjaïa is independent of Tunis. 'Al-Marīnī also confirmed that in the early 16th century, the emir of Béjaïa was independent of Tunis'; the page does not say when the separation began (the Hafsid dossier has no 1436-1500 event for it either); the page's 1436-1452 revolt of Abu-l-Hasan ended with Béjaïa captured by Uthman's troops on 9 November 1439, recaptured for about three weeks in 1446 and besieged again in 1452.

1510: Spain takes Béjaïa. Pedro Navarro reached Béjaïa on 5 January 1510 and the city fell to a general assault in late May (Arab sources: 5 Safar 915, 25 May 1510); the HB infobox gives 'Capture of Bejaia (1510): 9 November 1510'; an inscription on a Casbah door reads 1509. The Hafsid dossier has 1509.

1510: Emir Abderrahmane withdraws to the Kalaa. 'Emir Abderrahmane withdrew to the Kalâa of Beni Abbès and set up a principality' (the 1555 page gives no year; the Beni Abbas page: the kingdom 'owed its founding' to his withdrawal after the Spanish took Béjaïa in 1510).

1510: the emirate ends. The HB infobox lists the Capture of Bejaia (1510) as the end and names the Spanish Empire, the Kingdom of Kuku, the Kingdom of Beni Abbas and the Regency of Algiers as successors; the Capture page has Abu Bakr kill his brother Abdelaziz 'in battle at Takerkat' (no year) and take the title of sultan, while Abdelaziz's son Abbas sought Spanish help.

wars.name: Abu-l-Baqa's seizure of Tunis
wars.outcome: Abu-l-Baqa took Tunis in 1309 after seventeen days against the rival proclaimed there; a rebellion at Constantine led by his brother followed and he was assassinated; Abu Yahya Abu Bakr entered Tunis in early 1318 and reunited the Hafsid domains.
wars.note: The page gives no year for Abu-l-Baqa's fall.

wars.name: Abu'l Abbas's reunification of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Abu'l Abbas took Béjaïa from Abu Abdullah in May 1366 and reunited the western and eastern domains, for the third time, in 1370.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Béjaïa
wars.outcome: Pedro Navarro's expedition reached Béjaïa on 5 January 1510; the city fell in late May according to Arab sources; Sultan Abdelaziz's brother Abu Bakr, prince of Constantine, later killed him in battle at Takerkat (no year).

certainty.note: The page names towns and no frontier; whole provinces and 40-60 km circles are the researcher's. 1370-1500 has no shape (the branch is inside the unified Hafsid state) and 1501-1509 rests on one sentence of the page.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for this branch: the Hafsid Dynasty row (1236-1571) carries the Constantinois to 1555 (see the Hafsid dossier's notes). The sibling Hafsid dossier already holds this branch under the name 'Hafsid branch of Bejaia and Constantine' with a split in 1277, a merge in 1318 and a merge in 1370 (the last dated 1370 on both pages); the 1285 here is the infobox's, the 1277 the death of al-Mustansir. Gaps without a shape are deliberate: 1318-1349 and 1370-1500 the branch is inside the unified Hafsid state; 1351-1358 is the Marinid hold (the Hafsid dossier); the page gives no date for the cession to Abu Abdullah (1350 here is a bridge). The conflict of Béjaïa's fall: the HB infobox says 9 November 1510, the Capture page 25 May 1510 on Arab sources and 1509 on a door inscription; the Beni Abbas page gives 1510 and the Hafsid dossier 1509. The 1436-1452 revolt of Abu-l-Hasan (spring 1436 to 1439, capture of Béjaïa on 9 November 1439, three weeks of 1446, siege and betrayal in 1452) is the Hafsid dossier's war and is not drawn here. Constantine: the Capture page has a separate prince there in 1510, and the Hafsid dossier has it attached to Algiers in the 1530s. The page's Zayyanid and Marinid wars (Uthman's Zayyanids against Abu Zakariya; Abu Yaqub Yusuf's seizure of Algiers) have no year and are not drawn. The Kingdom of Kuku and the Kingdom of Beni Abbas dossiers (kingdom-of-kuku, kingdom-of-beni-abbas) cover the successors.
